papers.title: Toward a Quantum Information Foundation for Neutron Scattering
papers.abstract: Neutron scattering is a central probe of quantum materials, yet what quantum information can, in principle, be extracted from a scattering experiment remains unclear. Here we formulate neutron scattering as a quantum measurement, with the scattering amplitudes acting as Kraus operators on the material state. This provides a unified description of conventional intensity, coherent scattering, interferometric measurements, and entanglement witnesses, including those based on quantum Fisher information. We then ask how far this connection can be extended to nonlinear properties of a quantum state. For two independently prepared samples, we derive the general structure of probe-mediated measurement probabilities and show that, for spin-projection-conserving dynamics, low-order scattering cannot resolve certain many-body coherences required to determine purity. Conversely, an idealized single-spin protocol shows how probe-mediated exchange can access purity when the appropriate two-copy operation is realized. Our results establish a quantum-information description of neutron scattering and delineate the information accessible through conventional and interferometric measurements.

papers.title: Neutron star cooling with medium-modified Urca rates
papers.abstract: We study the effects of in-medium modification of the elementary cooling processes on observable properties of isolated neutron stars. We deduce the neutron star mass distributions compatible with the cooling analysis and compare with current theoretical models. We conclude that current cooling data require fast direct Urca cooling, moderated by proton superfluidity, to be active in most neutron stars, and that the DU onset threshold must lie below canonical masses. In that case medium modifications of modified Urca rates are practically insignificant, but the nn Bremsstrahlung rate plays a dominant role.

papers.title: Goldstone theory of gluon saturation in high energy QCD: From color glass to color superfluid condensate
papers.abstract: In the high energy Regge asymptotics of QCD, the rapid overpopulation of gluons leads to gluon saturation, characterized by nonperturbative semi-classical lumpy configurations of size $1/Q_S$, where $Q_S\gg \Lambda_{\rm QCD}$ is a dynamical semi-hard saturation scale. We discuss here a generalization of the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework describing this phenomenon that is obtained by carefully treating the breaking of global symmetries by the condensate. In particular, we show that the breaking of a global subgroup of color results in a Goldstone effective field theory (EFT) whose dynamics is characterized by a Goldstone decay constant $f_G = \sqrt{N} Q_S$, where $N=O(1/\alpha_S)$ is the phase space occupancy of the condensate, which is large for $\alpha_S(Q_S)\ll 1$. Further, the coupling of these colored Goldstones to collinear gluon modes leads to a depletion of the condensate, thereby modifying the static shockwave scattering framework of the CGC on timescales controlled by $f_G$. The CGC EFT on these longer time scales is a novel color superfluid. Low frequency modes with $\omega\leq \alpha_S Q_S$ in an external probe of the CGC are sensitive to superfluid dynamics, with interesting physical consequences for deeply inelastic scattering and ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions.

papers.title: Proton generalized parton distributions from electromagnetic form factors: A theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction
papers.abstract: We present a theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction of the unpolarized, chiral-even, leading-twist proton generalized parton distributions $H^q$ and $E^q$. At zero skewness, valence-quark distributions are combined with flavor-dependent exponential profiles calibrated simultaneously against phenomenological representations of the proton and neutron electromagnetic form factors. The construction imposes exact valence and anomalous-magnetic-moment normalizations, the low-scale condition $B^{u+d}(0)=0$, the required endpoint behavior, and the complete Gaussian impact-parameter positivity bound. The resulting parametrization provides a reasonable description of the electromagnetic form factors and their slopes while revealing the tension between strict GPD consistency and a precision reproduction of all low-$Q^2$ observables within the adopted ansatz. We extend the distributions to nonzero skewness using normalized double distributions and introduce an independent $D$-term to complete the relevant Mellin polynomials. We examine electromagnetic and energy--momentum-tensor form factors, impact-parameter distributions, positivity, polynomiality, and illustrative mechanical properties. The analysis distinguishes information constrained by electromagnetic data from additional assumptions governing skewness and the mechanical sector, thereby providing a transparent elastic baseline for future studies of nucleon-to-resonance transition GPDs.

papers.title: From lattice QCD thermodynamics to an effective quasiparticle description of gluonic matter at finite temperature
papers.abstract: We develop a lattice-constrained quasiparticle description of pure SU(3) Yang--Mills matter at finite temperature. The temperature-dependent effective gluon quasiparticle mass is determined from the lattice entropy density over $0.70\leq T/T_c\leq5$. It is interpreted as an effective thermal parameter encoding medium modifications of gluonic excitations, rather than as a physical gluon mass. With this mass fixed, we reconstruct the background contribution required for thermodynamic consistency, using a single pressure-normalization condition. The resulting pressure, energy density, entropy density, interaction measure, and squared speed of sound are then compared with available lattice results. Near $T_c$, the rapid variation of the effective mass is accompanied by a pronounced maximum in the interaction measure at $T/T_c\simeq1.09$, a strong suppression of the squared speed of sound, and a maximum in the background contribution. These correlated features characterize the substantial departure from conformal behavior in the transition region. At higher temperatures, the interaction measure decreases and the squared speed of sound approaches the conformal limit. We also examine the energy-per-excitation ratio $E/n_g$, which has a minimum of approximately $964~\mathrm{MeV}$ at $T/T_c\simeq1.21$. This ratio provides a measure of the excitation scale within the quasiparticle description. Overall, our results show how lattice thermodynamics can be mapped onto an effective gluonic excitation spectrum while maintaining thermodynamic consistency.

papers.title: Heavy quarkonium spin transport in a hot medium
papers.abstract: We investigate the in-medium spin transport of heavy quarkonium using an open-quantum-system approach based on potential nonrelativistic QCD. We express the heavy quarkonium dilepton decay angular distribution in terms of late-time quarkonium spin-dependent distribution functions. Working in the quantum-optical regime, where the inverse quarkonium size is much larger than the binding energy and the binding energy is comparable to or larger than the medium temperature $T$, we derive a spin-dependent quantum master equation incorporating both dissociation and regeneration, followed by the corresponding projected semiclassical Boltzmann equations. At leading order in the coupling, we retain the recoil corrections of relative order $T/M$ that contribute to the leading spin-dependent collision kernel. Here $M$ denotes the heavy-quark mass. At zeroth order in fluid gradients, we show that the relative motion between quarkonium and the medium supplies the leading anisotropy, while spin-chromomagnetic and spin-orbit interactions both contribute to the leading nonzero spin-alignment kernel. As an exploratory phenomenological application, we also estimate the medium-induced polarization parameter $\lambda_{\theta}$ of bottomonium $\Upsilon(1\text{S})$ using a simplified rate equation with background density matrices obtained from the Lindblad equation using QTraj. Within this simplified treatment, the resulting medium-induced polarization is found to be very small while a naive rescaling for charmonium can qualitatively describe the polarization of charmonium.

papers.title: Quantum computing for high energy nuclear physics
papers.abstract: Quantum information science (QIS) offers a new set of conceptual and computational tools ideally suited to exploring the many-body, out-of-equilibrium, and real-time properties of strongly interacting quantum systems. These themes find a natural counterpart in high energy nuclear physics, whose central goal is to describe the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction, under extreme conditions. Relevant examples range from the formation and internal structure of hadrons, to the collective and thermalization dynamics of strongly interacting QCD matter, and the properties of complex many-body scattering processes. Although tremendous progress has been made over the past decades in our understanding of QCD in the nuclear physics context, through perturbative methods, lattice QCD, and effective theory descriptions, phenomena that are intrinsically connected to real-time dynamics, highly entangled many-body evolution, or finite density regimes remain only partially accessible with existing approaches. In this article, we argue that QIS can help realize a new paradigm for addressing these open questions. With the aim of making the discussion accessible to both high energy nuclear physics and QIS audiences, we provide an overview of selected open problems in high energy nuclear physics, with emphasis on aspects motivated by collider phenomenology, and discuss how they can be approached using QIS tools. This connection is illustrated through representative examples drawn from the recent literature, making the case that QIS can become a driving force for discovery in nuclear physics in the coming years.

papers.title: Spurious center-of-mass mode as an $S$-matrix pole within the Jost-random-phase approximation
papers.abstract: Within the Jost-random-phase approximation (Jost-RPA), the spurious center-of-mass mode is a zero of the Jost determinant and hence a pole of the $S$ matrix. A zero at zero excitation energy $E$, whether from self-consistency or from a calibration of the residual interaction, is a pole of exactly second order when it has a single independent solution, every unoccupied bound orbital lies above the holes, and each hole is paired with every allowed partial wave; the order follows from the position of the zero, not from self-consistency. The state of this double pole, given by the Autonne-Takagi factorization of its $E^{-2}$ coefficient, is the zero-energy solution normalized by its inertia. In a self-consistent model of one energy density of the neutron and proton densities, every physical $S$-matrix element continued to $E=0$ carries the $E^{-2}$ term, contrary to an earlier conclusion. Subtracting the mode's principal part from the response changes the strength at real $E\neq0$ only through the smoothing and, in such a model, coincides with the projection of the ideal spurious state. In uncalibrated Woods-Saxon models of $^{16}$O and $^{208}$Pb the mode is a pair of poles on the imaginary axis.

papers.title: Interacting Boson System at Finite Temperatures: The treatment of the lattice QCD results
papers.abstract: We study an interacting relativistic system of charged bosons at finite temperature and fixed isospin density within a thermodynamically consistent mean-field approach. The interaction is represented by repulsive phi-4 and phi-6 self-interactions, which generate a density-dependent effective mass of the bosonic quasiparticles. We formulate the thermodynamics in the Extended Canonical Ensemble, obtained from the grand canonical description by a Legendre transformation from the isospin chemical potential to the conserved isospin density. In the condensed phase the chemical potential is constrained by the Bose-condensation condition and is therefore determined self-consistently through the effective mass. We apply the formalism to a pion-like system at finite isospin and clarify the relation between the isospin chemical-potential conventions used for pion and quark degrees of freedom. Using the convention adopted in lattice-QCD calculations, we compare the pressure, isospin density, energy density, and trace anomaly with lattice results at T=120 MeV. With one constant fitted to the lattice pressure, each model reproduces the lattice isospin density, energy density, and trace anomaly. Both the phi-4 and phi-6 models reproduce the main features of the lattice data, with the phi-6 interaction providing the better description. The Extended Canonical Ensemble provides a convenient framework for treating interacting particle-antiparticle systems across the transition to the Bose-condensed phase.

papers.title: Multi-phonon wobbling excitations as a probe for dynamical quasiparticle alignment
papers.abstract: The multiple and very extended triaxial strongly deformed bands of the $^{163,165}$Lu nuclei are used to ascertain the spin dependence of the odd quasiparticle alignment. The band heads are found to favor a tilted alignment geometry which gradually evolves into a transverse configuration. Distinct dynamical regimes are thus identified in specific bands and spin intervals, which are discussed in terms of wobbling excitations based on the analysis of the wave functions and $E2$ transition probabilities.

papers.title: Density-driven $\alpha$-particle clustering in neutron-rich oxygen isotopes
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the effect of valence neutrons on density-driven localisation in the neutron-rich oxygen isotopes. Calculations are performed within the multidimensionally constrained relativistic Hartree--Bogoliubov model using the DD-ME2 covariant energy-density functional. By constraining the mass rms radius to larger values, we study the structural evolution of these nuclei under progressive dilution, from spatially delocalised configurations to localised clustered states. The total energy, pairing correlations, deformation, and proton and neutron density distributions are analysed to determine how valence neutrons influence the emergence of $\alpha$-like clustering. For all three isotopes, we find a transition from a spatially delocalised nucleonic configuration to a tetrahedral $4\alpha$-like structure. The onset of this transition occurs at similar values of the radius-derived relative dilution parameter, $\chi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\rho_{\mathrm{PT}}/ \rho_{\mathrm{GS}}\simeq 0.28$--$0.31$, and shows only a weak dependence on neutron number. The excess neutrons modify the clustered density by increasing the density in the central regions and between clusters, while leaving the underlying tetrahedral core structure largely intact. Finally, we also use a phenomenological four-centre H\"uckel-type mapping of nuclei, which provides a molecular-orbital-like interpretation of cluster structures. We find that the effective coupling between the cluster centers decreases by progressively expanding the nucleus. The centroid-referenced energy shift $\Delta E_{\mathrm{val}}$ also becomes less negative and provides smaller net molecular-orbital-like energy lowering relative to its centroid with increasing neutron number.

papers.title: $\bar{D}$-meson Nucleon Scattering from Lattice QCD at the Physical Point
papers.abstract: We report the first lattice QCD study of the $s$-wave scattering of the $\bar{D}$-meson and the nucleon at the physical point, utilizing (2+1)-flavor configurations generated by the HAL QCD collaboration with a pion mass of $m_\pi\simeq 137$ MeV and a lattice spacing of $a\simeq0.084$ fm. By applying the HAL QCD method to the four-point correlation function of the $\bar{D}N$ system, we obtain a leading-order potential of the derivative expansion of the interaction kernel, which is then used to extract the $s$-wave phase shifts of low-energy $\bar{D}N$ scattering. Both the isospin $I=0$ and $I=1$ channels have a short-range repulsive core and a shallow attractive pocket in the intermediate to long-range region, though the $I=0$ channel is more attractive than the $I=1$ channel. We also observe that the $\bar{D}N$ potential exhibits more attraction than the $KN$ potential, which is its analog in the strange sector. In terms of the $s$-wave phase shifts, the $I=0$ channel shows a weak attractive behavior in the low-energy region with a positive scattering length of $0.425 \pm 0.163 (_{-0.105}^{+0.129})$ fm, whereas the $I=1$ channel shows repulsion with a negative scattering length of $-0.235 \pm 0.046 (_{-0.007}^{+0.040})$ fm. No bound states are found in both isospin channels, indicating the absence of a pentaquark state in the $s$-wave $\bar{D}N$ system.

papers.title: Scalar diquark mass and quark--diquark potential from lattice QCD using the potential method with a static quark
papers.abstract: We study the scalar diquark mass and the quark--diquark potential by applying a HAL QCD-inspired potential method to a baryonic system composed of a scalar diquark and a static quark. The diquark mass is determined self-consistently by requiring that the p-wave baryonic spectrum obtained from two-point correlators be reproduced within the potential framework. Numerical calculations are performed using $2+1$ flavor QCD gauge configurations generated by the PACS-CS Collaboration on a $L^{3} \times T = 32^{3} \times 64$ lattice with $a^{-1} \approx 2.176$ GeV and the pion mass, $m_{\pi} \approx 702$ MeV. From the analysis, we obtain a scalar diquark mass which is close to the na\"{\i}ve constituent quark estimate $ (2/3)m_{N}$, together with a quark--diquark potential of the Cornell type (Coulomb + linear). The string tension extracted from the quark--diquark potential agrees within approximately 5% with that obtained from the static quark--antiquark potential (Wilson Loop).

papers.title: Photon-nucleon entanglement in Compton scattering at low and high energies
papers.abstract: We study spin-spin entanglement in the final state photon-nucleon system in Compton scattering, both at low energy below the pion threshold and at high energy in perturbative QCD to next-to-leading order. We first establish a no-go theorem showing that, for any spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ target, entanglement cannot be generated in unpolarized Compton scattering if the scattering amplitudes are real. We then consider polarized Compton scattering off the electron, the proton and the neutron. At low energy, we uncover a rich variety of maximally entangled Bell states and their unitary equivalents realized across different regions of the kinematic plane. Interestingly, the proton and neutron targets exhibit distinct patterns of entanglement. In the neutron case, the electric and magnetic polarizabilities dramatically influence the pattern and even the existence of entanglement. This suggests that entanglement can serve as a novel tool for investigating the detailed electromagnetic properties of the nucleons.

papers.title: "Inevitable" nonstrange tetraquark states and $\rho\rho$ interaction
papers.abstract: Investigation of the interaction between two $\rho$ mesons with $IJ = 00,~02,~11,~20$ and $22$ is conducted systematically in the framework of the quark delocalization color screening model. The results show that there is a strong attractive potential between two $\rho$ mesons, which makes it easier for these two mesons to form bound states. The binding energies vary from a few MeV to over a hundred MeV. Moreover, the results of intercluster distances favor a molecular interpretation of these states. The interaction analysis reveals that the $\rho\rho$ and $\Delta\Delta$ interactions share certain similarities. Drawing inspiration from the $d^*$ dibaryon prediction and from decay-property analyses, we predict that the $\rho\rho$ with $IJ=02$ and $22$ are the most promising candidates of the ``inevitable'' nonstrange tetraquark states, which deserves experimental search.

papers.title: QCD phase structure at high baryon density
papers.abstract: Heavy-ion collisions provide unique access to the properties of QCD matter over a broad range of temperatures and baryon densities. We review recent progress in constraining the high-density phase structure of QCD, with particular emphasis on the microscopic inputs required for reliable transport modeling. We discuss cluster production, strange-particle interactions, collision dynamics at few-GeV energies, and the isospin dependence of the nuclear interaction, together with their impact on the interpretation of flow, yields, fluctuations, and possible critical signatures.

papers.title: Effects of in-medium $NN$ inelastic cross sections and the high-momentum tail of nucleon momentum distributions on pion production in heavy-ion collisions
papers.abstract: Pion production in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions (HICs) provides a sensitive probe of the nuclear equation of state and of the isospin dependence of reaction dynamics. In particular, pion production near threshold is strongly affected by the nucleon-nucleon ($NN$) inelastic cross sections and by the high-momentum components of the nucleon momentum distribution. To explore the influence of these two ingredients on pion production and charged-pion ratios, the in-medium $NN$ inelastic cross sections calculated within the relativistic Boltzmann-Uehling-Uhlenbeck transport theory and the short-range correlation induced high-momentum tail (HMT) are introduced into the Ultra-relativistic Quantum Molecular Dynamics model. By simulating Au+Au collisions at intermediate energies, we find that the in-medium modification of the $NN$ inelastic cross sections suppresses the pion multiplicity by reducing the probability of $N\Delta$ production in dense matter. The HMT, on the other hand, enhances the high-momentum components of nucleons and modifies the available energy in individual $NN$ collisions, thereby affecting $NN\rightarrow N\Delta$ reactions and the subsequent pion production. With the simultaneous inclusion of these two effects, the pion yields and the $\pi^-/\pi^+$ ratio data can be better reproduced. These results highlight the importance of both the in-medium reaction cross sections and short-range correlation induced high-momentum components in pion production in intermediate energy HICs.

papers.title: Characterizing $\pT$-differential Radial-Flow Fluctuations in Au+Au Collisions at FAIR with a Multi-Phase Transport Model
papers.abstract: We report the first predictions of the transverse-momentum ($\pT$)-differential radial-flow fluctuation observable, $\vzpT$, in Au+Au collisions at the top SIS100 energy, $\snn=4.9$~GeV, which will be available at the FAIR accelerator complex. Radial flow and its fluctuations are studied for different centrality intervals and reference-$\pT$ selections to investigate the properties and robustness of the calculated long-range correlation. $\vzpT$ displays a characteristic evolution from negative values at low $\pT$ to positive values at higher $\pT$. The integrated $v_0$, obtained with different reference-$\pT$ intervals, follows a common trend, with an approximately inverse-square-root dependence on the inclusive charged-particle multiplicity ($\nch$). The $\vzpT$ signal changes little when the pseudorapidity gap is varied between 0.2 and 0.8, or when the edges of the reference-$\pT$ interval are varied, in the bulk region. For identified particles, the pion and proton $\vzpT$ are ordered at low $\pT$, qualitatively similar to the mass ordering seen at higher energies. However, unlike at higher collision energies, $\vzpT$ does not exhibit constituent-quark number scaling, so the results do not support an interpretation in terms of partonic collectivity. The results are also in partial contradiction with the behavior of hadronic elliptic flow in these low-energy collisions. These results provide constraints on the evolution of radial correlations toward lower collision energies and motivate comparisons with complementary observables to clarify their connection to collective dynamics.
